text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: P1 runtime: host-prod serving queue depth > 95th pct of capacity and latency SLOs breached for text-gen models. Trigger: runtime.queue.depth alarm. link: https://internal/alarms/1841234567

maria.sre: ack - looking

maria.sre: initial triage: p75 tail latency for hosted-api spikes to ~2.4s, error rate up 4%. No obvious infra node OOMs. Load appears concentrated on long-running streaming responses for open-model zeta-13.

devon.platform: tagging: heavy_streaming_zeta13. Can you confirm if this is limited to hosted region us-east-1?

maria.sre: yes us-east-1 primarily, small spillover to us-west. Traffic peak is from a handful of high-throughput API keys (suspect customer churn test or bot).

ryan.runtime: (from runtime side) queue length growth suggests max_in_flight being saturated. Current max_in_flight per shard=400, avg inflight=390. KV cache hits fine. Backpressure not shedding yet.

sre-triage: @maria.sre @ryan.runtime can we throttle at edge while we investigate? Recommend immediate short mitigations: 1) temporary rate-limit heavy keys 2) lower max_in_flight to 200 on affected shards 3) disable streaming for zeta-13 on hosted tier (fallback to non-streaming).

maria.sre: agreed. Starting actions.

maria.sre: Action 1: identify top offending API keys
maria.sre: `SELECT api_key, count(*) as reqs, sum(tokens) FROM request_logs WHERE model='zeta-13' AND region='us-east-1' AND ts > now()-10m GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY reqs DESC LIMIT 20;`

maria.sre: top 3 keys are: key-A (92k reqs), key-B (48k), key-C (21k). These correlate with high concurrent streams.

devon.platform: Action 2: applying edge rate-limit via ingress config for those keys to 10 rps each. Patch to ingress:```yaml
# ingress patch
rate_limits:
  - api_key: key-A
    rps: 10
  - api_key: key-B
    rps: 10
  - api_key: key-C
    rps: 10
```

devon.platform: applied to edge in us-east-1, rolling config push started.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for ingress/ratelimit-config (rollout id: rl-184123)

maria.sre: Action 3: lowering runtime max_in_flight on affected shards. Command:```bash
rctl set runtime.max_in_flight --shards=\"shard-12,shard-13,shard-14\" --value=200
```

ryan.runtime: applied to shard-12/13/14. Monitoring queue depth.

maria.sre: Action 4: enable shedding for long-tail tokens for zeta-13: `runtime.flags.enable_token_shedding=true --model=zeta-13 --threshold=120s` (this will trim very long streaming sessions).

ryan.runtime: shedding flag toggled. Also bumped request timeout from 120s -> 45s on hosted tier for streaming endpoints as emergency mitigation.

cs-lead: CS heads up: we throttled three keys temporarily and reduced streaming timeout; customers on those keys will see rate-limited responses and possible cut streams. We'll notify top customers after stabilization.

maria.sre: Observed effects after ~30s: queue depth down 40%, p95 latency dropped to ~720ms, error rate trending down. Edge rate-limits tripped for key-A ~75% of requests, which is expected.

devon.platform: ingress rollout completed.

incident-bot: metrics-bot: alert resolved? runtime.queue.depth alarm cleared for us-east-1 at 1841234985

maria.sre: alarm cleared, but still above baseline. Need follow-up actions: 1) create playbook entry for automated rate-limits when sustained high queue persists 2) recommend permanent change to max_in_flight heuristics - make it dynamic by cpu/mem/latency, not static 3) add per-model streaming cost quota to prevent single model from dominating.

ryan.runtime: follow-up: we'll open RFC to add adaptive_max_in_flight that reduces max when sampler detects rising p95 and increases back via cooldown. Also add shedding policy tiers.

sre-triage: for immediate risk reduction, recommend we keep token timeout at 45s for next 4 hours and keep edge rate-limits in place for key-A/B/C. Set a 2h runbook to restore if stable.

maria.sre: agreed. I'll file an incident summary and SLA impact assessment. Preliminary CS impact: 3 customers affected (key-A/B/C) reduced throughput, <0.5% of total customers. Estimated error budget burn: 0.8% of hosted-prod SLA this week.

cs-lead: I'll draft outbound note to the three customers explaining that we detected abnormal traffic and applied temporary limits; we'll follow up with root cause.

devon.platform: NOTE: when we lower max_in_flight in runtime, some requests returned 503s for short window while shards applied change - seen ~150 5xx in logs. We'll include that in postmortem.

maria.sre: handoff plan: I'm on call for next 30m to monitor recovery. @ryan.runtime please take over if it reoccurs after I sign off. If it resurfaces, escalate to incident lead.

ryan.runtime: ack, standing by.

maria.sre: incident state -> mitigated. I'll update incident tracker with timeline and actions.

sre-triage: Followups assigned: #1 create adaptive_max_in_flight RFC (owner: ryan.runtime), #2 edge automatic throttling playbook (owner: devon.platform), #3 per-model cost quotas (owner: product). ETA 2 weeks for RFCs, playbook MVP in 3 days.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 1841235267

maria.sre: quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely a misconfigured client test creating sustained high-concurrency streaming sessions against zeta-13; mitigations worked but we need faster automatic throttles and adaptive runtime backpressure to prevent manual interventions.

devon.platform: logging action: add a new histogram for per-key concurrent streams so we can trigger automated throttling earlier.
